items.statement: Direct transfer to CT on the ambulance stretcher with a single group page on pre-alert will reduce the median door-to-needle time from 62 to 45 minutes or less within six months, without more symptomatic haemorrhage or more than 5 percent treated mimics.
items.rationale: The largest delays are in the steps these changes target (c1, c2); novelty is low, which suits local improvement.
items.risks: CT conflicts with trauma; out-of-hours cases improve less.

items.statement: Preparing the thrombolytic during the CT scan saves about 7 minutes per case.
items.rationale: Late drug preparation added a median of 7 minutes in time studies.
items.risks: Drug wasted when the scan excludes treatment.

items.statement: A nurse-led two-minute debrief after each case sustains the gains.
items.rationale: Debriefs were feasible and seen as blame-free elsewhere.
items.risks: Effect not separable from other changes.

summary: Three hypotheses; h1 selected for the first cycles.
